name: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) - Outpatient / Mild
commonOrganisms: Viral (RSV, Influenza, hMPV), Streptococcus pneumoniae, Group A Streptococcus, H. influenzae, Mycoplasma pneumoniae
comments: Antibiotics are not routinely recommended if viral infection is suspected. For bacterial suspicion in outpatient setting, high-dose Amoxicillin is preferred. Review at 48 hours.

antibiotics.label: High-dose Amoxicillin (Preferred)
antibiotics.doseText: 80 - 90 mg/kg/day PO in 2 to 3 divided doses (max. 1g/dose, 3g/day)
antibiotics.notes: NAG 2024 & WHO endorse weight-band dosing to streamline prescribing and minimize calculation errors. Safe wide therapeutic index.

antibiotics.label: Erythromycin Ethylsuccinate (Alternative / Penicillin Allergy)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 50 mg/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses (max. 800mg/dose, 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Macrolide is indicated if Mycoplasma pneumoniae or Chlamydia is suspected, or in non-severe penicillin allergy.

antibiotics.label: Azithromycin (Atypical Pathogens / Alternative)
antibiotics.doseText: 10 mg/kg/day PO OD (max. 500mg/day) on Day 1, then 5 mg/kg/day PO OD (max. 250mg/day) on Days 2-5
antibiotics.notes: Convenient once-daily dosing. Use for suspected atypical pneumonia.

antibiotics.label: Amoxicillin/Clavulanate (Augmentin 7:1) (If Beta-lactamase producer suspected)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 50 mg/kg/day (amoxicillin component) PO in 2 divided doses (max. 2g amoxicillin/day)
antibiotics.notes: Take with meals to minimise gastrointestinal adverse effects.

name: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) - Inpatient / Moderate-Severe
commonOrganisms: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus, Group A Streptococcus, H. influenzae
comments: Blood cultures prior to antibiotics. Switch to oral antibiotics once child is afebrile for 24-48h and clinically improved.

antibiotics.label: Ampicillin IV (First-line Inpatient)
antibiotics.doseText: 150 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Preferred empiric parenteral therapy for fully immunized children without empyema or severe necrotising features.

antibiotics.label: Benzylpenicillin (Penicillin G) IV
antibiotics.doseText: 200,000 units/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 24 million units/day)
antibiotics.notes: High efficacy against susceptible pneumococcus.

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV (Severe / Unimmunised / Sepsis)
antibiotics.doseText: 150 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Indicated if child is critically ill, not fully vaccinated against Hib/S. pneumoniae, or with pleural effusion.

antibiotics.label: Ceftriaxone IV (Alternative Inpatient / Once Daily)
antibiotics.doseText: 50 - 80 mg/kg/day IV in 1 to 2 divided doses (max. 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Avoid concurrent calcium-containing IV solutions. Do not use in neonates with hyperbilirubinaemia.

antibiotics.label: Cloxacillin IV (Add if Staph aureus suspected / Cavitary / Empyema)
antibiotics.doseText: 100 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Add if Staphylococcus aureus is clinically suspected (rapidly progressive pneumonia, pneumatoceles, empyema).

name: Empyema Thoracis / Parapneumonic Effusion
commonOrganisms: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus, Group A Streptococcus
comments: Diagnostic thoracocentesis & chest drain insertion required. Continue IV antibiotics until chest tube removed and fever resolved, then switch to oral.

antibiotics.label: Ampicillin/Sulbactam IV (Unasyn)
antibiotics.doseText: 150 - 200 mg/kg/day (ampicillin component) IV in 4 divided doses (max. 8g ampicillin/day)
antibiotics.notes: Broad coverage including anaerobic and beta-lactamase producing organisms.

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV PLUS Cloxacillin IV
antibiotics.doseText: Cefotaxime 150-200 mg/kg/day IV q6h-q8h + Cloxacillin 100-200 mg/kg/day IV q6h
antibiotics.notes: Covers both Gram-negative/pneumococcal pathogens and MSSA.

antibiotics.label: Vancomycin IV (If MRSA suspected or critical sepsis)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 60 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/day). Monitor trough level.
antibiotics.notes: Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) mandatory. Target trough level: 10-15 mcg/mL (or 15-20 mcg/mL in severe disease).

name: Acute Pyelonephritis / Febrile UTI (≥3 months)
commonOrganisms: Escherichia coli (80%), Klebsiella spp., Proteus mirabilis, Enterobacter spp.
comments: Obtain clean-catch or catheter urine culture prior to starting antibiotics. Duration: 7 to 10 days. Switch to oral once afebrile for 48h.

antibiotics.label: Cephalexin PO (First Line Oral)
antibiotics.doseText: 25 - 50 mg/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses (max. 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Appropriate for mild to moderate pyelonephritis tolerating oral intake.

antibiotics.label: Amoxicillin/Clavulanate PO (Augmentin 7:1)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 50 mg/kg/day (amoxicillin component) PO in 2 divided doses (max. 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Formulation 7:1 (228mg/5mL or 457mg/5mL). For Formulation 14:1, dose is 80-90 mg/kg/day.

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV (Hospitalized / Toxic / Vomiting)
antibiotics.doseText: 150 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 3 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 6g/day)
antibiotics.notes: First-line parenteral option for sick febrile UTI / pyelonephritis. May add Amikacin if septic shock.

antibiotics.label: Ceftriaxone IV / IM (Daily Inpatient / Outpatient Parenteral)
antibiotics.doseText: 75 - 100 mg/kg/day IV/IM in 1 to 2 divided doses (max. 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Convenient once-daily dosing. Switch to oral stepdown when afebrile.

antibiotics.label: Amikacin IV (Add if septic or suspected resistant GNB)
antibiotics.doseText: 15 mg/kg/dose IV once daily (q24h) (max. 1.5g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Once-daily extended interval aminoglycoside dosing. Monitor renal profile.

name: Lower Urinary Tract Infection (Acute Cystitis)
commonOrganisms: Escherichia coli, Proteus mirabilis, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Staphylococcus saprophyticus
comments: Afebrile child with dysuria, frequency, or urgency. Short-course therapy is effective. Duration: 3 to 5 days.

antibiotics.label: Amoxicillin/Clavulanate PO (Augmentin 7:1) (Preferred)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 50 mg/kg/day (amoxicillin) PO in 2 divided doses (max. 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Excellent urinary penetration. Standard 7:1 oral suspension.

antibiotics.label: Cefuroxime Axetil PO
antibiotics.doseText: 30 mg/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses (max. 250mg/dose, 500mg/day)
antibiotics.notes: Take with food to increase absorption and mask bitter taste.

antibiotics.label: Co-trimoxazole (Bactrim) PO
antibiotics.doseText: 8 - 10 mg TMP/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses (max. 160mg TMP/dose, 320mg TMP/day)
antibiotics.notes: Check local antibiogram for E. coli resistance. Contraindicated in G6PD deficiency with severe hemolysis history and neonates.

antibiotics.label: Nitrofurantoin PO (Alternative)
antibiotics.doseText: 2 mg/kg/dose PO q12h (sustained-release) or 1 mg/kg/dose PO q6h (immediate-release) (max. 100mg/dose)
antibiotics.notes: For lower UTI only! Ineffective for pyelonephritis due to low tissue/renal parenchyma levels. Contraindicated if CrCl < 30 mL/min or G6PD deficiency.

name: Acute Bacterial Meningitis (Infant & Child ≥3 months)
commonOrganisms: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, Haemophilus influenzae type b
comments: Medical emergency! Start empiric therapy immediately after blood culture. Do NOT delay antibiotics if lumbar puncture is postponed. Add Dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg IV q6h before or with first dose for Hib/pneumococcal meningitis.

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV (Preferred First Line Meningitic Dose)
antibiotics.doseText: 200 - 300 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 12g/day)
antibiotics.notes: High CNS penetration. Continue for minimum 10-14 days for S. pneumoniae, 7 days for N. meningitidis.

antibiotics.label: Ceftriaxone IV (Alternative Meningitic Dose)
antibiotics.doseText: 100 mg/kg/day IV in 1 to 2 divided doses (max. 4g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Can give as 100mg/kg OD or 50mg/kg q12h. Highly potent.

antibiotics.label: Vancomycin IV (Combine if Cephalosporin-resistant Pneumococcus suspected)
antibiotics.doseText: 60 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/day). Target trough 15 - 20 mcg/mL.
antibiotics.notes: Add routinely if PRSP (penicillin/cephalosporin-resistant S. pneumoniae) is suspected or patient is in septic shock.

antibiotics.label: Ampicillin IV (Add if Listeria monocytogenes suspected)
antibiotics.doseText: 300 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 12g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Indicated in immunocompromised children or infants < 3 months for Listeria coverage.

name: Neonatal Early-Onset Sepsis / Meningitis (≤ 7 days of life)
commonOrganisms: Group B Streptococcus (GBS), Escherichia coli, Listeria monocytogenes, Enterococcus
comments: Empiric combination therapy with Ampicillin + Aminoglycoside (Gentamicin) or Cefotaxime. Adjust Gentamicin dosing interval by gestational age (GA/CGA)!

antibiotics.label: Ampicillin IV (Neonatal Sepsis)
antibiotics.doseText: 100 - 150 mg/kg/day IV in 2 divided doses (q12h if ≤7 days; if meningitis: 200-300 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses)
antibiotics.notes: For meningitis, increase to 200-300 mg/kg/day divided q12h (if ≤7 days) or q8h (if >7 days).

antibiotics.label: Gentamicin IV (Neonatal Gestational-Age Regimen)
antibiotics.doseText: 5 mg/kg/dose IV. Frequency: <30w CGA: q48h; 30-34w CGA: q36h; ≥35w CGA: q24h
antibiotics.frequency: Stratified by Gestational Age (<30w: q48h, 30-34w: q36h, ≥35w: q24h)
antibiotics.notes: NAG 2024 CGA protocol. Monitor serum trough level (<1-2 mcg/mL) and peak level (5-10 mcg/mL).

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV (Alternative to Gentamicin or if Meningitis proven)
antibiotics.doseText: 50 mg/kg/dose IV. Frequency: ≤7 days PNA: q12h; >7 days PNA: q6h-q8h (max. 200mg/kg/day)
antibiotics.notes: Safe in neonates; does not displace bilirubin from albumin (unlike Ceftriaxone which is contraindicated in neonates).

name: Neonatal Necrotising Enterocolitis (NEC - Stage 1 to 3)
commonOrganisms: Klebsiella spp., E. coli, Clostridia, CoNS, Enterococci, Bacteroides spp.
comments: Bowel rest, NPO, gastric decompression, fluid resuscitation and prompt triple broad-spectrum coverage.

antibiotics.label: Ampicillin IV (Stage 1 NEC)
antibiotics.doseText: 100 mg/kg/dose IV. Frequency: ≤1 week of age: q12h; >1 week of age: q8h
antibiotics.notes: Combine with Gentamicin + Metronidazole for Stage 1.

antibiotics.label: Gentamicin IV (NEC Stage 1)
antibiotics.doseText: 5 mg/kg/dose IV (<30w CGA: q48h; 30-34w CGA: q36h; ≥35w CGA: q24h)
antibiotics.notes: Can substitute with Amikacin 15mg/kg/dose if local Gram-negative resistance is high.

antibiotics.label: Metronidazole IV (Anaerobic Coverage for NEC)
antibiotics.doseText: Loading: 15 mg/kg IV once. Maintenance: ≤34w: 7.5 mg/kg q12h; 35-40w: 7.5 mg/kg q8h; >40w: 10 mg/kg q8h
antibiotics.notes: Crucial anaerobic gut flora coverage for bowel wall ischemia/necrosis.

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV (NEC Stage 2 / Stage 3 - In place of Amp+Gent)
antibiotics.doseText: 50 mg/kg/dose IV. Frequency: ≤1 week of age: q12h; >1 week of age: q8h (PLUS Metronidazole)
antibiotics.notes: Preferred for established pneumatosis intestinalis or perforation.

name: Skin & Soft Tissue: Impetigo / Mild Cellulitis / Folliculitis
commonOrganisms: Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA), Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A Strep)
comments: For localized impetigo, topical mupirocin 2% or fusidic acid is first line. If extensive or associated with systemic symptoms/cellulitis, use oral anti-staphylococcal therapy.

antibiotics.label: Cephalexin PO (First-Line Oral)
antibiotics.doseText: 25 - 50 mg/kg/day PO in 2 to 4 divided doses (max. 500mg/dose, 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Pleasant suspension taste compared to oral cloxacillin; excellent compliance in children.

antibiotics.label: Cloxacillin PO (Oral Anti-Staphylococcal)
antibiotics.doseText: 50 - 100 mg/kg/day PO in 4 divided doses (max. 500mg/dose, 2g/day) 1 hour before food
antibiotics.notes: Administer on an empty stomach. Highly bitter syrup; advise child/parent.

antibiotics.label: Amoxicillin/Clavulanate PO (Augmentin 7:1)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 50 mg/kg/day (amoxicillin) PO in 2 divided doses (max. 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Broad coverage for animal/human bites, or secondary infection of eczema.

antibiotics.label: Clindamycin PO (Severe Penicillin Allergy or suspected CA-MRSA)
antibiotics.doseText: 20 - 30 mg/kg/day PO in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 450mg/dose, 1.8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Inhibits toxin synthesis in Group A Strep and S. aureus.

name: Severe Cellulitis / Erysipelas / Staphylococcal Scalded Skin Syndrome (SSSS)
comments: Mark border of erythema with pen to monitor progression. Switch to oral therapy once erythema recedes and fever resolves for 48h.

antibiotics.label: Cloxacillin IV (First-Line Parenteral)
antibiotics.doseText: 100 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Gold standard for Methicillin-Susceptible S. aureus (MSSA) and SSSS.

antibiotics.label: Cefazolin IV (Alternative Parenteral)
antibiotics.doseText: 50 - 100 mg/kg/day IV in 3 divided doses (max. 1g/dose, 3g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Excellent tolerability with convenient 8-hourly dosing.

antibiotics.label: Vancomycin IV (Suspected MRSA or Type 1 Penicillin Anaphylaxis)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 60 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/day). Monitor trough level.
antibiotics.notes: Target trough: 10-15 mcg/mL. Infuse over at least 60 minutes.

name: Acute Otitis Media (AOM)
commonOrganisms: Streptococcus pneumoniae, non-typeable H. influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, Viral
comments: Watchful waiting (48-72h) recommended if ≥2 years with mild unilateral symptoms. High-dose Amoxicillin is preferred to overcome intermediate penicillin-resistant S. pneumoniae.

antibiotics.label: High-Dose Amoxicillin PO (Preferred First Line)
antibiotics.doseText: 80 - 90 mg/kg/day PO in 2 to 3 divided doses (max. 1g/dose, 3g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Duration: 10 days for age <2 years; 5-7 days for age ≥2 years.

antibiotics.label: Amoxicillin/Clavulanate (Augmentin 7:1) (AOM Treatment Failure / Purulent conjunctivitis)
antibiotics.doseText: 80 - 90 mg/kg/day (amoxicillin) PO in 2 divided doses (max. 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Indicated if child received amoxicillin in past 30 days or failed to improve after 48-72 hours.

antibiotics.label: Cefuroxime Axetil PO (Non-severe Penicillin Allergy)
antibiotics.doseText: 30 mg/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses (max. 250mg/dose, 500mg/day)
antibiotics.notes: Second-generation cephalosporin for non-IgE penicillin allergic patients.

antibiotics.label: Azithromycin PO (Severe Type 1 Penicillin Allergy)
antibiotics.doseText: 10 mg/kg/day PO OD on Day 1 (max. 500mg), then 5 mg/kg/day PO OD on Days 2-5 (max. 250mg)
antibiotics.notes: Reserve for true beta-lactam anaphylaxis.

name: Acute Streptococcal Pharyngotonsillitis (GAS)
comments: Routine antibiotic treatment is NOT indicated for viral sore throat (majority of cases). Test with rapid antigen or Centor/McIsaac score. Goal: prevent acute rheumatic fever and suppurative complications.

antibiotics.label: Penicillin V (Phenoxymethylpenicillin) PO (First-Line)
antibiotics.doseText: < 27 kg: 250 mg PO q8h or q12h; ≥ 27 kg: 500 mg PO q8h or q12h for 10 full days
antibiotics.notes: Must complete full 10-day course to prevent Rheumatic Fever.

antibiotics.label: Amoxicillin PO (Alternative First-Line - Better Taste)
antibiotics.doseText: 50 mg/kg/day PO once daily (OD) or in 2 divided doses (max. 1g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Once daily or twice daily dosing improves compliance. Complete 10 days.

antibiotics.label: Cephalexin PO (Penicillin Allergy - Non-severe)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 50 mg/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses (max. 500mg/dose, 1g/day)
antibiotics.notes: First-generation cephalosporin for non-Type 1 allergic patients.

antibiotics.label: Erythromycin Ethylsuccinate PO (Severe Penicillin Allergy)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 mg/kg/day PO in 2 to 4 divided doses (max. 1g/day)
antibiotics.notes: For patients with true immediate IgE penicillin hypersensitivity.

name: Acute Bacterial Gastroenteritis / Dysentery (Bloody Diarrhoea)
commonOrganisms: Shigella spp., Salmonella (non-typhoidal), Campylobacter jejuni, E. histolytica
comments: Oral rehydration is paramount! Antibiotics are NOT routinely indicated for acute watery diarrhoea. Indicated only for macroscopic blood in stool (dysentery), systemic toxicity, severe malnutrition, or high-risk infants.

antibiotics.label: Azithromycin PO (First Line for Shigellosis & Campylobacter)
antibiotics.doseText: 10 - 12 mg/kg/day PO OD for 3 days (max. 500mg/day) OR 20 mg/kg single dose
antibiotics.notes: First choice in children. High intracellular tissue concentrations and short course.

antibiotics.label: Ceftriaxone IV (Severe / Toxic / Sepsis / Unable to take oral)
antibiotics.doseText: 50 - 75 mg/kg/day IV once daily (max. 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Parenteral therapy for children with severe dehydration, bacteraemia or inability to tolerate oral medications.

antibiotics.label: Metronidazole PO (If Amoebic Dysentery / E. histolytica suspected or Giardiasis)
antibiotics.doseText: 30 - 40 mg/kg/day PO in 3 divided doses (max. 500mg/dose, 1.5g/day)
antibiotics.notes: For trophozoites seen in stool microscopy or proven amoebic colitis.

name: Paediatric Sepsis & Septic Shock (Community-Acquired)
commonOrganisms: Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus, Group A Streptococcus, Enterobacterales
comments: CRITICAL: Administer empiric intravenous antibiotics within the first hour of recognition ('Golden Hour'). Take blood cultures before starting antibiotics without delaying infusion.

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV (Preferred First Line Sepsis)
antibiotics.doseText: 150 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Third-generation cephalosporin covering encapsulated organisms and GNB.

antibiotics.label: Ceftriaxone IV (Alternative Sepsis First Line)
antibiotics.doseText: 80 - 100 mg/kg/day IV in 1 to 2 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 4g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Convenient once or twice daily infusion. Avoid calcium co-administration.

antibiotics.label: Cloxacillin IV (Add for Staphylococcal toxic shock or purpura)
antibiotics.doseText: 100 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Add if staphylococcal sepsis or toxic shock syndrome suspected.

antibiotics.label: Gentamicin IV (Add for synergistic Gram-negative coverage in shock)
antibiotics.doseText: 7.5 mg/kg/dose IV once daily (q24h) (max. 400mg/day). Monitor trough level.
antibiotics.notes: Once daily extended interval dosing for synergy. Trough target < 1 mcg/mL.

antibiotics.label: Vancomycin IV (Add if MRSA risk or central venous catheter sepsis)
antibiotics.doseText: 45 - 60 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/day). Target trough 15 - 20 mcg/mL.
antibiotics.notes: Target trough: 15-20 mcg/mL for severe sepsis / bacteraemia.

name: Melioidosis (Burkholderia pseudomallei) (Updated Jan '26)
comments: Two-phase therapy: Intensive IV phase (minimum 10-14 days; longer if deep organ abscesses or neuromelioidosis) followed by Eradication oral phase (minimum 12 weeks with Cotrimoxazole).

antibiotics.label: Ceftazidime IV (Intensive Phase - First Line)
antibiotics.doseText: 150 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 6g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Intensive phase. Infuse over 30-60 minutes.

antibiotics.label: Meropenem IV (Intensive Phase - Severe Sepsis / Neuromelioidosis)
antibiotics.doseText: 75 - 120 mg/kg/day IV in 3 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 6g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Preferred in septic shock or neuromelioidosis. Extended infusion over 3 hours optimizes time above MIC.

antibiotics.label: Co-trimoxazole (Bactrim) PO (Eradication Phase)
antibiotics.doseText: 8 - 10 mg TMP/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses with Folic Acid supplement (5mg/day)
antibiotics.notes: Eradication phase to prevent relapse. Co-prescribe Folic acid 5mg daily. Monitor FBC and renal profile.
